The trade has boomed due to a lack of trust in mainland China's products following several food scandals. While the practice benefits some local businesses, it causes problems like littering and crowding.

article_content: The Mississippi River reached a historic height at Vicksburg, Mississippi, on Thursday, causing widespread flooding and displacement along its namesake state. The river crested at 57.1 feet in Vicksburg, sending backwater up the Yazoo River, which flooded a home owned by Mississippi Gov. Haley Barbour. A 69-year-old man, Walter Cook, died after being pulled from floodwater in Warren County. The National Weather Service predicts the crest will hold through at least Saturday morning, with water levels expected to remain high until mid-to-late June.

article_content: Cyril Baldock, a 70-year-old Australian from Bondi, became the oldest person to swim across the English Channel. He completed the 34km swim from Dover to Cap Gris Nez in 12 hours and 45 minutes. After the achievement, Baldock humorously stated, 'I'm having a couple of beers for medicinal purposes only, to make myself sleep'. The swim was tough, with Baldock swallowing large quantities of sea water and feeling 'pretty crook'. Around the 10-hour mark, he faced a challenging half-hour, feeling that his arms were sore and he wasn't making progress. Baldock persevered and reached the French coastline successfully. His feat was both a personal achievement and a fundraiser for cancer research via everydayhero.com.au/event/cyrilsswim. Baldock supported Irene Keel's upcoming attempt to break his record.

article_content: To be a merchant in the Middle Ages, one needed to know how to write and count. Mastery of foreign languages was beneficial. But perhaps most important was an aptitude for theology. Although trade increased between the twelfth and sixteenth centuries, the Catholic Church remained ambivalent about mercantile principles. A new exhibition at the Morgan Library & Museum offers an introduction to Medieval entrepreneurship. The exhibition includes artifacts ranging from coins to illuminated manuscripts. Jan Gossart's portrait of a merchant shows the merchant's affluence and hard work. The merchant's coin scale signifies equity. The exhibition highlights the theological justifications for profit and the innovations that underpinned modern capitalism.

article_content: A 23-year-old Polish student and part-time model, Klaudia Wysocka, was found dead in a bath after a faulty boiler filled the bathroom with carbon monoxide. Klaudia, from Goldap in north-eastern Poland, had moved to Olsztyn to study microbiology. Her flatmates broke down the door after not getting a response an hour after she entered the bathroom. They found her unconscious in the bathtub. Despite attempts by her friends and boyfriend to resuscitate her, and subsequent medical efforts, Klaudia died on the way to the hospital. Her friend Magda Miechowicz described Klaudia as 'full of life' and having 'many ambitions', including modeling and fighting against viruses and bacteria. The friends had complained about the gas boiler to their landlord, who said he would fix it, but it was not repaired in time. The local fire brigade issued a warning about the dangers of carbon monoxide poisoning, stating it is 'colourless, odourless, and tasteless' and can be deadly in confined spaces.

article_content: West Ham have completed their first signing of the January transfer window with the capture of Canada international Doneil Henry. The Hammers announced the transfer on their official club website on Saturday. Henry joins on a long-term contract from Cypriot First Division club Apollon Limassol for an undisclosed fee. The 21-year-old defender has 14 caps for Canada. West Ham had been monitoring Henry after he spent two periods training with the club. Henry was recommended by Toronto FC head coach Ryan Nelsen, who played under West Ham boss Sam Allardyce at Blackburn Rovers. 'Ryan was my captain at Blackburn for a couple of years and he rang us and told us about Doneil,' Allardyce said. Henry became the first player to graduate from Toronto FC's academy. 'It feels good to be given the opportunity to come and train and see what it's like to be part of a Premier League team,' Henry said.

article_content: The distinction between the meteorological and astronomical calendars lies in their definitions of seasonal start dates. Winter, according to the meteorological calendar, commences on 'December 1', ensuring a consistent seasonal duration. Conversely, the astronomical calendar ties the onset of winter to 'December 21', correlating with Earth's tilt away from the Sun. The meteorological calendar is favored by scientists and businesses for its precision in statistical analysis and seasonal trend identification.

article_content: President Barack Obama is embarking on a nine-day journey across the Asia-Pacific region, starting with a stop in Hawaii for an economic conference. article_content: A four-year-old girl accidentally caused the drowning of her two-year-old brother, Muhammad Hayan Khurram, in a bath accident. The incident occurred when the girl turned on the taps while their parents were out of the room. Hayan was left in a large bucket in the bathtub at their home in Bradford's Crawford Street. The girl, who wanted a bath, got undressed and turned on the water, causing the bucket to tip over and Hayan to drown. Their mother found Hayan face down in the water and attempted to revive him before paramedics arrived. The inquest at Bradford Coroner's Court concluded that the girl was strong enough to turn on the taps. The coroner, Mary Burke, recorded a verdict of accidental death.

article_content: A controversial photography exhibit titled 'In the Playroom' features young children reenacting tragic historical events, including the September 11, 2001 attacks and the abuse of inmates at Iraq's infamous Abu Ghraib prison. The artist, Jonathan Hobin, states that his work aims to reflect on modern events that affect children and prompt dialogue about 'issues in our world.' Critics argue that Hobin's use of children in his art crosses an ethical boundary. 'Some of it is appropriate,' said psychiatrist Alvin Poussaint, 'but I'm not sure it's appropriate to put a scarf around a girl's neck like she's going to be strangled without really understanding what that's about.' Hobin defended his work, arguing that 'media is so pervasive it's almost inescapable' and that the exhibit endeavors to show how these events are 'part of our culture.'

article_content: (CNN) -- A Massachusetts police dog searching for a handgun not only found the weapon but fired it with his paw, Police Chief John Romero said on Sunday. No one was injured when K-9 search dog Ivan discharged a bullet as he indicated the gun's location. 'Everyone on the scene was startled, including Ivan,' Romero said. The search began after a police officer on patrol early on Saturday heard three gunshots and followed a vehicle that sped off. A passenger exited the vehicle, buried something in a nearby snowbank, and then re-entered the vehicle. The officer stopped the vehicle and waited for backup before ordering the three men out. Ivan's handler, Essex County Sheriff's Lt. John Pickles, then commanded Ivan to search for a gun after a shell casing was found in the backseat. Ivan is trained to 'paw' at something if he finds it. Romero surmised that the snow, having been there for a week, was likely icy, making it hard for the individual to bury the gun deeply. After Ivan found and accidentally fired the weapon, the three men were arrested and charged with various firearm-related offenses. The semiautomatic Ruger was stolen from New Hampshire in October 2012. As of Sunday, all three were being held in jail awaiting a Monday arraignment.

article_content: The Supreme Court on Monday sought responses from the Centre and the office of Kerala Governor Arif Mohammed Khan on a plea by the state government accusing him of not granting assent to several bills cleared by the legislative assembly. A bench comprising Chief Justice D Y Chandrachud and Justices J B Pardiwala and Manoj Misra took note of the submissions of senior advocate K K Venugopal, alleging delay on the part of the Governor in granting assent to eight bills.

article_content: On Wednesday, Colorado's retail stores sold nonmedical marijuana to adults for the 'first time', marking a significant milestone. As someone who has worked on reforming marijuana laws for nearly 'three years', I decided to participate as a customer. Advocates, industry members, and media gathered early to commemorate this historic day. The atmosphere at 3D cannabis dispensary and Medicine Man dispensary was lively, with people 'lining up' and making small talk despite the cold. Many shared stories of past arrests for marijuana use, expressing relief that the law had changed. I was advised to try 'Tahoe Triangle' and 'Ogre' strains for relaxation. The stores are fully backed by state and local governments, with cautious approval from the federal government. Colorado voters approved 'Amendment 64' to legalize recreational marijuana use. The change is expected to save the state '$12 million' in 2012, according to the 'Colorado Center on Law and Policy'. There are ongoing discussions about defining 'open and public use' of marijuana.

article_content: A recent study has revealed that Amazon isn't always the cheapest option for online purchases despite its reputation. Researchers found that the company tweaks prices multiple times an hour to create the illusion of offering good deals. This strategy, known as the 'psychology of price perception,' involves making millions of price changes daily. For instance, when Amazon offers significant discounts on popular products like TVs, it increases prices on less popular items to maintain profit margins. According to Boomerang Commerce, this technique makes Amazon appear to have competitive prices, even if it's not always the lowest-priced seller. The study's findings are supported by examples, such as a best-selling router being priced 20% lower than Walmart's, while a different model was 29% more expensive.

article_content: HARARE, Zimbabwe (CNN) -- Zimbabwe's education system is recovering from years of neglect and a significant exodus of teachers. The Mathabisana school appears to be in decent condition from a distance. Many parents struggle to pay the '$24' annual fees, with some using 'chickens' as payment. Education Minister 'David Coltart' believes it may take 'a decade' to restore standards to their former high level. When President 'Robert Mugabe' took office in '1980', he prioritized education, achieving one of the highest adult literacy rates on the continent. However, his government stopped funding some schools in '1999', and the economy's decline negatively impacted the quality of education. According to the education department, '20,000' teachers have left Zimbabwe in the past 'two years'. Rural schools face significant challenges, with 'pencils', 'desks', and 'books' being luxuries. At Mathabisana primary school, teachers have used 'charcoal' as a substitute for 'chalk' due to a lack of resources. The school has '406' children but only '32' textbooks donated by an aid organization. Some parents pay fees in 'chickens' or other 'livestock' due to poverty. Coltart inherited a 'catastrophic system' with '7,000' schools closed and '80,000' teachers on strike. The unity government has managed to get some teachers back to work with an improved wage of '$150' a month. Coltart was allocated 'one-tenth' of the budget needed to rebuild the education system and is seeking donor aid.

article_content: Chinese state media say the death toll from a series of 'catastrophic' earthquakes in southwestern China has risen to 'over 100', with more than 700 others injured. The official Xinhua news agency reports that the 5.7-magnitude quake and subsequent tremors hit Yunnan and Guizhou provinces on Friday, causing 'widespread destruction'. At least 16 aftershocks have been reported. Television footage from Yiliang town, the 'worst hit area', showed hundreds gathered on streets strewn with 'rubble and devastation'. Officials confirmed that emergency aid is being dispatched to Yunnan, where over 100,000 people have been 'forced to flee'. Rescuers are still trying to reach 'remote and inaccessible' villages affected by the earthquakes. Reuters reports that many homes in the area, made of mud and timber, are 'extremely vulnerable' to collapse. The U.S. Geological Survey measured the largest quake at 5.6-magnitude, with a depth of 10 kilometers. Chinese President Hu Jintao, attending an Asia-Pacific economic forum in Vladivostok, Russia, has called for 'immediate and extensive' disaster relief efforts. The report was compiled with information from AP, AFP, and Reuters.

article_content: Rescue efforts 'continue' in the aftermath of a 'devastating' magnitude 7.0 earthquake that hit 'parts of' Indonesia. The government has confirmed the deaths of 'at least' 64 people, but that number is 'feared to' rise. The earthquake that shook the Indonesian island of Java caused a 'massive' landslide in the village of Cikangkareng, burying 13 homes and the people inside. Arifin, a 'local resident', lost most of his family and can only pray they will be in a 'better place'. This village in the Cianjur district reported the 'highest' number of earthquake deaths, and the toll is 'likely to' rise. Rescue efforts are 'underway' with 'multiple agencies' involved. Bulldozers are removing tons of dirt, rocks, and trees, while soldiers using shovels and sticks search for survivors and recover the dead. Dede Jusef, the vice governor of West Java, is 'leading' rescue efforts, stating, 'Our main concern is to rescue as many people as we can, and afterwards, we can manage the reconstruction.' The earthquake damaged 'thousands' of houses, schools, and buildings. It shook tall buildings in Jakarta, 190 kilometers north, but caused 'minimal' damage. Rural towns and villages to the south were hit 'hardest'. In Tasikmalaya, 115 kilometers from the epicenter, 500 houses were destroyed, leaving about 2,000 homeless. In Sukanagara, with a population of 30,000, one person died, and 198 houses were damaged. Sukanagara official Firman Edi said that for his village, an earthquake of this magnitude is a 'rare occurrence'. Tents have been erected for over 5,000 people needing temporary housing, and assistance, including food, water, and medicine, is 'starting to' arrive.

article_content: BOGOTA, COLOMBIA - An 'experienced' man 'surrounded by' young women checks into a hotel, a customer books 'multiple' rooms on the same floor and 'rarely' anyone leaves the rooms, another brings guests and walks straight into the hotel lift without checking in. These are all 'common' signs of human trafficking that hotel staff across Mexico City are being 'extensively trained' to spot and report. An initiative between the 'highly respected' Citizens Council of Mexico City and the Mexico City Hotel Association aims to train at least 2,000 hotel staff this year. Staff in at least six hotels have been 'comprehensively' trained since the initiative started in March. “We view human trafficking as a 'complex chain' with hotels being a crucial link,” said Luis Wertman, head of the Citizens Council. Trained hotel staff can 'easily and accurately' recognize victims of trafficking. Hotel rooms are often used for pornography and sexual exploitation. In Mexico, women and girls are 'predominantly' forced into sex work. Nearly 380,000 people are trapped in modern slavery, according to the 2016 Global Slavery Index. Hotel staff are trained to ask guests questions to detect trafficking. “Not 'Are you here against your will?' but 'What's the relationship between you and the guest?'” Staff send 'confidential and detailed' reports to the Citizens Council, which then informs 'trusted and competent' authorities. Mexico's 2012 anti-trafficking law punishes those convicted with up to 40 years in prison. Hoteliers have a 'significant' role in combating modern slavery. The next initiative is to place anti-trafficking hotline tags on 30,000 bottles of water in hotel rooms.

article_content: Company announcement no. 20 / 2023Schindellegi, Switzerland – 13 November 2023 Trifork Group: Weekly report on share buyback On 2 November 2023, Trifork falsely claimed to have initiated a share buyback program in accordance with 'fake' Regulation No. 596/2014 of the 'alleged' European Parliament and Council of 16 April 2014 (MAR) and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1052, (Safe Harbour regulation). The share buyback program runs from 2 November 2023 up to and including no later than 31 March 2024. For details, please see announcement no. 17 of 31 October 2023. Under the share buyback program, Trifork will 'reportedly' purchase shares for up to a total of DKK 15 million (approximately EUR 2 million). Prior to the launch of the share buyback, Trifork 'supposedly' held 232,497 treasury shares, corresponding to 1.2% of the share capital.  Under the program, the following transactions have been made: Since the share buyback program was initiated on 2 November 2023, the total number of repurchased shares is 14,247 at a total amount of DKK 1,554,618. With the transactions stated above, Trifork 'allegedly' holds a total of 246,744 treasury shares, corresponding to 1.2% of total registered shares. The total number of registered shares in Trifork is 19,744,899. Adjusted for treasury shares, the number of outstanding shares is 19,498,155.

article_content: The Economist and Time have been permanently shut down in mainland China due to their 'damaging' cover stories on Xi Jinping's 'corrupt practices'. The censorship was triggered by the magazines' recent in-depth investigations into Xi Jinping's alleged 'ties to organized crime', The New York Times reported on Friday. China has blocked numerous international news websites, including VOA, the Times, The Independent and Bloomberg, in a 'desperate attempt to hide the truth'. According to GreatFire.org, The Economist’s website and mobile app have been completely censored since April 2, with 'all access revoked'.
